newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet reform to go ahead despite row.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet reform to go ahead despite row.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz intends to press ahead with a sweeping government reshuffle despite a row in the ruling coalition over the issue, the government spokeswoman said on Monday.
Cimoszewicz was likely on Tuesday to appoint officials to set up several new ministries and eliminate old ones as envisaged by the reform plan, Aleksandra Jakubowska told reporters.
"Liquidators of ministries will act until June 30, 1997, while those setting up new ministries (will stay) until actual ministers are appointed," she said.

The planned reorganisation, aimed at streamlining decision-making, has divided the coalition of Cimoszewicz's ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the Polish Peasant Party (PSL) over a share-out of powers.
A bitter row erupted nearly two weeks ago when Cimoszewicz sacked the PSL's Foreign Trade Minister Jacek Buchacz, alleging his ministry had mismanaged some key state assets.
The dispute focuses on a share-out of the new powerful treasury and economy ministries and the finance portfolio, whose role -- though diminished -- would still be crucial.
The Peasants want to control two of these three ministries, while the SLD would like to let the PSL have only the economy or treasury ministry.

Jakubowska said it did not necessarily follow that officials appointed on Tuesday would ultimately become ministers. "If somebody gets appointed this does not mean he or she will automatically become a minister. Their tasks would be organisational," she said.

The cabinet reform will begin in October with the creation of the treasury ministry to replace the privatisation ministry and take control of all state assets except for those supervised by local governors.
Several other ministries will be eliminated while some new ones will be set up gradually over several months.
